solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Regularly smash fairway to create one endless sand trap!

indicators.note: regularly tells us to take every other letter of the words smash fairway, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A golfer's exclamation about a long fairway shot ending up in an enormous bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: The golfing picture makes 'sand trap' look like a bunker; here it is a whole desert that never seems to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast desert is jokingly a sand trap without limits, the world's biggest bunker.

clue.text: What frozen birds do and I do is fly badly

indicators.note: flying badly suggests the letters of I do is fly tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A whimsical comparison between frozen birds and a poor flyer.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of I DO IS FLY gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds that freeze harden into a solid mass, which is the verb meaning to become hard.

clue.text: Deliveries may be staggered

parts.note: in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled; one struck clean over the boundary is sent flying, and 'staggered' hints at being knocked reeling

explanation.surface: A notice that parcels or post may arrive at different times.
explanation.walkthrough: Deliveries reads as post; in cricket it means balls bowled, and a big blow that sends one over the boundary unbounced scores six runs. 'Staggered' also suggests something reeling from a heavy blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket idiom for striking a ball over the boundary without bouncing, scoring six, figuratively a staggering blow.

clue.text: French ways to express regrets

definitions.meaning: streets in France are called by this word

explanation.surface: A remark on how the French voice their regrets.
explanation.walkthrough: One word is both the French for streets and an English verb for regretting.
explanation.definitionFit: French for streets, and an English verb for lamenting or feeling sorry about something.

clue.text: Enjoying luxury, including your sweetheart

parts.note: inc. is the standard abbreviation for including
a sweetheart is a lover

explanation.surface: Living the good life, with your beloved along too.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for living in comfort and prosperity, like cattle grazing in a rich pasture.

clue.text: It's deadly with no end to tax and debts

indicators.note: the end of the word tax means its final letter

parts.note: IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A grim view of a life without taxes but with debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmful or poisonous, as a deadly gas is described.

clue.text: Rugby team includes gentler men like Daniel

indicators.note: includes means the team's name holds the other piece within it

parts.note: the British and Irish Lions are a touring rugby team
tamer means gentler, less wild

explanation.surface: A rugby squad picks some softer players resembling a man named Daniel.
explanation.walkthrough: Daniel survived the lions' den in the Bible, so he is presented as a handler of the big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel calmed the lions in the biblical den, so he stands as an example of such animal handlers.

clue.text: A weakness to hide love, say

indicators.note: to hide something is to cover it up inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a vice is a weakness of character
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone with a failing who conceals a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to express or utter something aloud in words is a synonym of say.

clue.text: Controller of programmes is standoffish

definitions.meaning: the handset used to change TV channels

explanation.definitionFit: A TV handset controls which programmes are shown; distant in manner also means aloof.

clue.text: Take exception to a certain article

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to protest; as a noun it is a specific thing or item.

clue.text: What security-conscious Spooner has fitted to front door

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swaps the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: a householder worried about burglars wants better security fittings
what that householder has fitted is locks

explanation.surface: A careful householder named Spooner installing something on his front door.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone security-conscious fits BETTER LOCKS; swapping the opening sounds gives the slot the post comes through.
explanation.definitionFit: The slot for post is a fixture set into a front door.

clue.text: Number in wars with China

definitions.meaning: read as numb-er, a thing that numbs: a narcotic
Britain fought the nineteenth-century wars named after this drug against China

explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but something that numbs; Britain fought two wars with China in the 1800s over trade in this drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic numbs pain, and the drug trade caused two nineteenth-century conflicts with China.

clue.text: Humour about the Last Trump

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a humour is a mood, as in good humour

explanation.surface: A joke about the final trumpet blast, or about a certain politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The Last Trump is the trumpet call announcing Judgment Day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Trump heralds the Day of Judgment, which is the end of the world or final fate.

clue.text: To expel people takes time for such conduct

parts.note: to deport is to expel from a country
men are people

explanation.surface: Expelling people slowly is described as a kind of behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing or behaviour; how a person carries themselves is their conduct.

clue.text: Sounds like appropriate gift is a cheap ornament!

indicators.note: sounds like says the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to appropriate is to nick, steal; a gift or talent is a knack

explanation.surface: Someone sniffy about a present being a tacky trinket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is the verb to nick (steal), not the adjective 'suitable'; a gift is a knack.
explanation.definitionFit: A small worthless decorative trinket is a cheap ornament.

clue.text: Fabric woven from finest end of cloth

indicators.note: weaving interlaces threads, so these letters are interlaced into a new order
the end of the word cloth is its last letter

explanation.surface: A material made from the finest last scraps of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' takes the H from cloth, which is mixed in with FINEST.
explanation.definitionFit: An open mesh fabric used for stockings is a type of textile.

clue.text: The south gets more than enough,for instance

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A remark that southern England is well supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen or example is given for instance, as one case standing for many.

clue.text: Lie around, definitely relaxed

indicators.note: around suggests moving the letters of lie about into another order

parts.note: surely means definitely

explanation.surface: Lounging about is plainly a restful pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' is the anagram signal on 'Lie', not a word meaning nearby; 'definitely' supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurried and easy-going in pace, the way a relaxed stroll is taken.

clue.text: Engine is not to be broken up for scrap

parts.note: a jet is a type of engine

indicators.note: broken up tells us the letters of is not are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanic deciding an engine should be sent for scrap rather than dismantled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be broken up' rearranges IS NOT into TISON.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to throw overboard or discard is to scrap something.

clue.text: Weapon carried around by Private Cox, evidently

indicators.note: around means the hidden letters are read in the opposite direction
carried means held within, so the answer's letters are hidden inside these words

explanation.surface: A soldier named Private Cox seen carrying a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carried' takes TECOXE from inside 'Private Cox, evidently', and 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-made anti-ship missile, a well-known guided weapon.

clue.text: I am enthralled by slim-making vitamin

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: making slim is to make thin

explanation.surface: Someone captivated by a diet supplement promising weight loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamin B1 is known by this name, a member of the vitamin family.

clue.text: The colour of Crimean bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters of Crimean go wild

explanation.surface: Musing on what shade bananas from the Crimea might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivid crimson-red is a named colour, a shade of red.

clue.text: Like a cougher, perhaps (or a "coffer", you might say)

definitions.text: Like a cougher, perhaps (or a "coffer", you might say)

parts.words: Like a cougher, perhaps (or a "coffer", you might say)
parts.note: someone with a cough has a congested chest; a coffer is a chest, and cougher sounds like coffer

explanation.walkthrough: Cougher and coffer sound alike, and a coffer is a chest, so the bracket offers a second route to the same adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes someone with bronchial congestion, and jokingly something resembling a treasure box.

clue.text: Transport sector to go in convoy

indicators.note: transport means carry away, so the letters of sector are moved about

explanation.surface: The haulage industry travelling in a line of lorries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like a noun for the haulage business but signals rearranging SECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany someone for protection, as warships guarding a fleet of ships do.

clue.text: Hoards supplies and lots of cash

parts.note: stock means supplies held
piles of money means lots of cash

explanation.surface: Someone stashing away goods and plenty of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate and store up reserves is a synonym of the verb hoard.

clue.text: Gulf Arab in a second uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second

explanation.surface: An Arab from the Gulf joining a revolt in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: IN A MO ('in a second') read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Oman, a country on the Arabian Gulf coast.

clue.text: Smash and grab in a police raid

definitions.meaning: to break, as in ... a window
a drugs ... is an arrest or seizure in a raid

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for breaking something, and for a raid or arrest made by police.

clue.text: He joins the Gunners but can't go on the wing

indicators.note: joins here means enters, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, whose soldiers are gunners

explanation.surface: A recruit joining an artillery regiment, or Arsenal FC (nicknamed the Gunners), but unable to play out wide.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunners is also Arsenal's nickname, so 'on the wing' looks like a football position; it means flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A large South American flightless bird, like an ostrich, so it cannot fly.

clue.text: Former leading man gets old by degrees

parts.note: BA and MA are university degrees, Bachelor and Master of Arts

explanation.surface: An ageing film star slowly getting older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading man' suggests an actor; here it is a former US president, and 'by degrees' gives two qualifications rather than meaning gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: A past US president was the nation's leader, so a former leading man.

clue.text: Like the top team without a fixture

explanation.definitionFit: Means unequalled, like a side that beats everyone, and literally lacking a scheduled game.

clue.text: It couldn't describe Henry VIII's judgment

parts.note: Henry VIII was famously fat, so slim could never describe him
Henry VIII was a king of England

explanation.surface: A historian's comment on the decisions of a much-married Tudor king.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII was notoriously stout, so the clue's phrase 'thin king' could never be applied to him.
explanation.definitionFit: One's opinion or view, as in 'to my way of reasoning', is one's judgment.

clue.text: Indian tree hiding outlaw and any criminal

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of any are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: A fugitive and some crook sheltering in an Indian tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges ANY into YAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fig tree native to India whose aerial roots form new trunks.
